title: Metric aliasing & canonicalization + dashboard mapping playbook
content:
Summary:
This doc is a working playbook for consolidating metric aliases into a small canonical metric set and mapping those canonical metrics to dashboard tiles and trace anchors. Goal is to reduce panel duplication, improve SLI stability, and make investigation flows (metric -> trace -> span) deterministic across teams.

Context and motivation:
- Over time multiple services and SDK versions emitted slight variants of the same logical signal (examples below). Dashboards have proliferated the variants as separate panels; alert noise and oncall confusion increased.
- We want a pragmatic, low-risk migration path: keep old metrics writable for a transition window but surface canonical names everywhere and adopt aliasing rules in query libraries and dashboards.

Examples of current alias patterns (real observed):
- token_latency_ms, tok_lat_ms, latency.tokens.ms
- kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_hits_pct, kvcache.hit_rate
- model.request.count, requests_model_v2, model_infer_calls

High-level principles:
1) Keep canonical names short, imperative, and tool-agnostic (no SDK prefixes, no retention hints). E.g., inference.tokens.latency_ms, cache.kv.hit_rate, model.requests.count.
2) Use dot-delimited hierarchy: <domain>.<entity>.<measure>[_units]. Prefer snake or dot? Use dot for hierarchy and underscore for units.
3) Single source-of-truth alias map in telemetry repo: a small CSV/TSV mapping old_name -> canonical_name + rationale + owner.
4) Backwards compatible: ingestion accepts existing names and tags them with canonical via processing layer. Dashboards should query canonical names by default.
5) Alert rules and SLIs must only be attached to canonical metrics. Exceptions require a documented risk note.

Canonicalization mechanics (implementation sketch):
- In the ingestion/metrics pipeline (metrics-shim component): run an alias lookup for metric.name and remap to canonical_name tag (not renaming the timestamped series). The raw metric continues to exist to avoid breaking producers.
- The query layer (promql/sql wrapper): expose a view called metrics.canonical that rewrites queries to select either canonical_name or apply coalesce across aliases during transition. Example: coalesce(metric{canonical=~"inference.tokens.latency_ms"}, metric{__name__=~"tok_lat_ms|token_latency_ms"})
- Short-term: dashboards will use a thin query library helper in the frontend (grafana macros) to expand aliases. Long-term: replace macros with canonical queries once alias emitting stops.

Dashboard mapping rules (operator/ux guidance):
- Every dashboard tile must include: canonical metric, alias list (hidden as panel notes), owner contact, query version tag, expected baseline (how to interpret the number).
- Panel naming conventions: <Product area> — <Canonical metric> — <Slice>. Example: Serving — inference.tokens.latency_ms — p50/p95/p99.
- Avoid panels that mix alias names. If a legacy team insists on a legacy panel, flag it as Transitional and add a TTL tag.

Tracing linkage rules:
- Each canonical metric should define a trace anchor: the dominant span name or tag to link to. Store as part of the alias map file: canonical_name -> trace_anchor_pattern.
- When an alert hits on canonical metric, the incident template should include the tracing query for that anchor pre-filled (span name + span.tag filter). Example: span.name =~ "model.infer.*" and span.tag.model_id = $model_id
- Instrumentation checklist for new metrics: include trace_anchor, session_id propagation hooks, and span IDs in logs. Without anchor, metric cannot be a primary SLI.

Migration plan (phased):
Phase 0: Inventory (2 weeks)
- Run alias discovery job across telemetry for the last 2 years to build candidate map. Output CSV with frequency, cardinality, producer service. (Owners: Jonah + Diego)

Phase 1: Canonicals chosen & master map (1 week)
- Workshop with owners to pick canonical names for top 40 metrics by volume. Add owners and rationale. Publish to github telemetry/metric-aliases.csv.

Phase 2: Query helpers + dashboard mapping (2–3 weeks)
- Implement grafana macros + prometheus view for coalescing aliases. Update templates for central dashboards to use canonical. Add panel notes listing aliases.

Phase 3: Producer coordination + transition window (8–12 weeks)
- Owners add canonical emission to new SDKs. We monitor alias vs canonical ratios. Migration guardrails: 95% canonical for 4 consecutive weeks to consider retiring alias panels.

Phase 4: Sunset & cleanup (2 weeks)
- Remove aliases from templates and mark old panels archived. Keep alias-to-canonical map for audit history.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Investigation quick-card: When latency SLO breach detected on inference.tokens.latency_ms -> run pre-canned trace query on trace_anchor, then fetch last 50 requests with session_id and prefix warm status.
- Alert triage template: Always cite canonical metric, list alias matches observed, and whether they were included in alert calculation.

Open questions / risks:
- Cardinality explosion if we create canonical tags incorrectly (owner tag granularity?), need strict owner review.
- Cross-cloud naming collisions (same raw name in different accounts) — add namespace prefix at ingestion layer as fallback.
- How to surface canonical vs. alias in external customer dashboards (exposing canonical is preferred for support consistency).

Action items (short):
- Jonah: run inventory job and create initial alias CSV by 2025-11-17.
- Priya: prototype grafana macro for coalesce queries, draft PR by 2025-12-01.
- Diego: add trace_anchor column to telemetry schema and prototype incident template by 2025-12-08.

Notes to self / work-in-progress style:
- Keep this doc light; expect iterated versions. Follow-up session scheduled w/ infra + SDK folks next Friday.
- Potential follow-up: automatic DB of historical alias mappings for alert retrospective analysis.

References and links: see linked_artifacts for current PR and Jira. Also ping #obs-telemetry in Slack (thread pinned: "metric-canonicalization-2025").

End of draft.
